quick: 0.5 mL intramuscular single dose each season (age-/product-specific)
Recommended in any trimester (inactivated - safe in pregnancy)
Observe for immediate allergic reactions; injection-site reactions
summary: Inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV) provides active immunization against the influenza A and B strains it contains. It is non-infectious (split-virion or subunit) and is given as an annual seasonal dose, intramuscularly in most products, to protect against influenza disease. Standard adult dosing is 0.5 mL IM once per season; children 6 months through 8 years who are not previously primed may need two doses. It is recommended in pregnancy and during breastfeeding. The main concern is hypersensitivity; the standard-dose IIV does NOT cause influenza because it contains no live virus.
indications: Active immunization for the prevention of influenza disease caused by the influenza A subtype and type B virus strains contained in the vaccine, in eligible persons per age indication

dosage.n: Annual revaccination with the current season's formulation

dosage.d: Two doses (0.25 or 0.5 mL per product) at least 4 weeks apart
dosage.n: Single dose in subsequent seasons / if previously primed

dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM; high-dose or adjuvanted IIV preferentially recommended
dosage.n: Enhanced products may improve response in older adults

admin: Administer intramuscularly (deltoid in adults/older children; anterolateral thigh in infants) - do not inject intravascularly
Inspect for particulates/discoloration and shake prefilled syringes/vials before use as directed
Use the current season's vaccine and the age-appropriate product and volume
Have epinephrine and equipment for anaphylaxis immediately available; observe after injection
Can be co-administered with other vaccines at separate sites
moa: Inactivated influenza vaccine contains non-infectious split-virion or subunit antigens (chiefly hemagglutinin) from the influenza A and B strains predicted for the season. It stimulates the host to produce strain-specific antibodies, predominantly anti-hemagglutinin antibodies, that neutralize the virus and prevent or attenuate influenza illness on subsequent exposure. Because the virus is inactivated, the vaccine cannot cause influenza.

absolute: Severe allergic reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis) to a previous dose of any influenza vaccine or to any vaccine component
relative: Moderate or severe acute illness with or without fever (defer until recovery)
History of Guillain-Barre syndrome within 6 weeks of a prior influenza vaccine
Egg allergy - any severity may receive age-appropriate flu vaccine (per ACIP); severe egg allergy in a setting able to manage reactions

preg: Recommended. Inactivated influenza vaccine is safe and recommended in any trimester of pregnancy; vaccination protects the mother and provides passive protection to the infant in the first months of life.
lact: Recommended and safe during breastfeeding; it does not pose a risk to the nursing infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment; standard immunization in renal impairment, though immune response may be somewhat reduced.

moderate: Immunosuppressive therapy (high-dose corticosteroids, chemotherapy, biologics) - may blunt the immune response
minor: May be given with other inactivated or live vaccines at separate anatomic sites
interactions.diagnostics: Can cause transient false-positive serologic tests (e.g., HIV, HCV, HTLV-1) shortly after vaccination.

rare: Shoulder injury related to vaccine administration (improper technique)
emergency: Signs of anaphylaxis - difficulty breathing, throat/face swelling, hives, hypotension

monitoring: Observe for immediate allergic reactions after administration (and for syncope)
Document lot number and administration per immunization records
counsel: This is the flu shot - it cannot give you the flu because the virus is inactivated
You need it every year because the strains and your immunity change
Sore arm, mild aches or low fever for a day or two are normal
It is recommended and safe in pregnancy and while breastfeeding
Tell the provider about any severe allergic reaction to a previous flu vaccine; seek urgent care for swelling, trouble breathing or hives after the shot
pk: Protective antibodies develop ~2 weeks after vaccination
Antibody titers peak within several weeks
Not applicable - immunization, not a small-molecule drug
Protection wanes over the season; annual revaccination needed
Store refrigerated at 2-8 C; DO NOT freeze; protect from light
pearls: Inactivated - it does not contain live virus and cannot cause influenza
Recommended annually for essentially everyone >=6 months, including pregnant women in any trimester
Children 6 months-8 years who are vaccine-naive need 2 doses >=4 weeks apart the first season
Egg-allergic persons of any severity can receive age-appropriate flu vaccine per ACIP
For adults >=65, high-dose or adjuvanted formulations are preferentially recommended
missed: Influenza vaccine is given once per season; there is no daily dose to miss. If you have not been vaccinated, get it as soon as possible - vaccination remains beneficial throughout the influenza season. Children needing a second priming dose should receive it about 4 weeks after the first.
overdose: Overdose is not expected with single-dose presentations. Inadvertent administration of more than the recommended volume would, at most, increase local injection-site or systemic reactogenicity; manage symptomatically.
